themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints spiked 194% this week (29 complaints vs. 9.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks), suggesting a concentrated wave of code enforcement issues or unreported violations in CD 405, coinciding with 414 DOB permits filed in last 90 days including 43 new buildings and 8 demolitions.
evidence: Building/Use complaints: 29 last week vs. 9.9 weekly average (z-score: 9.43, highest statistical significance)
414 DOB permits filed in last 90 days, including 43 new buildings and 8 full demolitions
Community Board has repeatedly requested additional building inspectors—unmet need for 1+ year
reporting_angles: Are contractors and developers cutting corners during active construction? Interview DOB and recent permit holders.
Is the city's building inspection capacity overwhelmed? Investigate inspector staffing levels vs. permit volume in CD 405.

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints nearly doubled this week (17 complaints vs. 7.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks, up 134%), marking a sharp escalation in pest pressure across the district, potentially linked to construction activity and infrastructure work.
evidence: Rodent complaints: 17 this week vs. 7.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.24, high statistical significance)
134% spike occurred over same period as Building/Use and hazmat spikes, suggesting construction-related attractants
No recent community board or media coverage of rodent issues—emerging blind spot
reporting_angles: Are ongoing construction projects (43 new buildings, 8 demolitions) creating gaps in waste management or attracting rodents?
Talk to residents in blocks with highest permit activity—are they seeing increased rodent activity near work sites?

themes_detail.label: Air Quality & Environmental Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints surged 276% this week (8 complaints vs. 2.1 weekly average), while hazardous materials complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 1100% above baseline (3 complaints vs. 0.2 average), together signaling potential air pollution and contamination concerns tied to demolition or industrial activity.
evidence: Air quality complaints: 8 this week vs. 2.1 weekly average (z-score: 5.04)
Hazardous materials complaints: 3 complaints three weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35, 1100% spike)
8 full demolitions filed in DOB permits—likely source of dust, asbestos, lead paint concerns
reporting_angles: Are demolition sites following air quality protocols? Request 311 complaint addresses and cross-reference with DOB demolition permits.
Is there a specific industrial or commercial facility generating hazmat complaints? Map the 3-complaint hazmat cluster from 3 weeks ago.

themes_detail.label: Street & Curb Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, complaints about root/sewer/sidewalk condition (11 complaints, up 144% vs. 4.5 average) and curb condition (8 complaints, up 300% vs. 2.0 average) have surged in parallel, suggesting concentrated infrastructure failure in specific blocks, compounded by long-term community board requests for sewer inspection and repair.
evidence: Root/Sewer/Sidewalk complaints: 11 two weeks ago vs. 4.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.81, up 144%)
Curb condition complaints: 8 last week vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.9, up 300%)
Community Board has filed same budget request for 'Inspect sanitary sewer on specific street segment and repair or replace as needed' year after year—suggests known problem area.
reporting_angles: Which street segments are concentrating these complaints? Request 311 complaint geo-data and interview residents on the hardest-hit blocks.
Has DEP inspected the flagged sewer segments? Why has the community board's repeated funding request gone unfulfilled?

themes_detail.label: Safety Incidents Double
themes_detail.summary: Safety complaints tripled 2 weeks ago (11 complaints vs. 2.8 weekly average, up 300%), marking a distinct departure from baseline, though the category is broad; investigate whether this reflects criminal activity, hazardous conditions, or both.
evidence: Safety complaints: 11 two weeks ago vs. 2.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.58, up 300%)
No corresponding Reddit discussions, local news mentions, or council constituent cases—potential coverage gap
Timing overlaps with Building/Use and Rodent spikes, suggesting environmental hazards (construction, unsecured sites) may be driving safety calls
reporting_angles: Request 311 safety complaint descriptions and addresses from 2 weeks ago—are they tied to construction sites, abandoned buildings, or crime?
Are there common themes (e.g., unsafe scaffolding, open pits, unsecured demolition sites) that could be addressed by DOB enforcement?
